findings.claim: The negative harness never exercises two of the three platform-react-boundary triggers: no fixture is a `.tsx` file under `platform/`, and no fixture imports plain `react`, so a regression that deletes the `file.endsWith(".tsx")` branch or narrows the react regex would still pass the harness and CI.
findings.evidence: Criterion 5.2 requires 'negative fixtures that prove each platform-adapter rule rejects a violation', but the only React-boundary fixture is `scripts/fixtures/platform-adapters/platform/react-dom.ts` (a `.ts` file importing `react-dom/client`); `expectedRules` only asserts the rule name appears, so one trigger firing satisfies the test for all three.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `scripts/fixtures/platform-adapters/platform/widget.tsx` (JSX, no react import string needed beyond the transform) and a fixture importing `"react"`, and assert the violating file names appear in output so each trigger is independently proven.

findings.claim: Retired-path rules only match the exact legacy prefixes (`protocols/agui-`, `lib/db`, `lib/pglite-assets`), so the retired entry points can silently return in directory form such as `protocols/agui/index.ts` or `lib/pglite/client.ts`.
findings.evidence: The regexes `/^(?:@\/|.*\/)protocols\/agui-/` and `/(?:^|\/)lib\/(?:db|pglite-assets)(?:\.ts|\/|$)/` require the literal `agui-`/`db`/`pglite-assets` segment; `protocols/agui/` and `lib/pglite/` match neither the import checks nor the file checks.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the retired-path patterns to cover the namespaces, e.g. `protocols/agui(?:-|\/|$)` and `lib/(?:db|pglite)(?:[-.\/]|$)`, and add a negative fixture for a directory-form retired path.

findings.claim: The scan filter `/\.(ts|tsx)$/` lets `.js`/`.jsx` files under `frontend/src` or `frontend/e2e` bypass every rule, including direct PEM imports and React usage inside `platform/`.
findings.evidence: The repo already contains plain-JS config at the frontend root (`frontend/vite.config.js` in the file tree), so JS files in the tree are a realistic occurrence; the gate's only file filter is `walk(scanRoot).filter((file) => /\.(ts|tsx)$/.test(file))`.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the filter to `/\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mts|cts)$/` or document why JS sources are out of scope for this gate.

findings.claim: The dynamic-import regex `import\s*\(\s*["']` misses specifiers preceded by a comment, so `await import(/* chunk */ "@prometheus-ags/prometheus-entity-management")` evades the sole-facade rule.
findings.evidence: `/\bimport\s*\(\s*["']([^"']+)["']\s*\)/g` requires the quote immediately after optional whitespace; any `/* ... */` between `(` and the quote prevents a match, and no negative fixture covers dynamic PEM imports at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow comments in the pattern (e.g. `import\s*\(\s*(?:/\*[^*]*\*/\s*)*["']`) or flag any `import(` in scanned files whose specifier cannot be extracted.

findings.claim: The static-import regex matches the words `import`/`export` inside comments and string literals, so a test or fixture embedding a code sample like `"import { x } from '@/lib/db'"` would trip the gate with a false positive and block CI on unrelated content.
findings.evidence: `/\b(?:import|export)\s*(?:[^"'`;]*?\bfrom\s*)?["']([^"']+)["']/g` runs over raw file content with no comment/string awareness; a string literal containing `import ... from '@/lib/db'` yields the module `@/lib/db` and a `retired-pglite-import` violation.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip line/block comments and quoted strings before matching, or require the match to start at a statement boundary (line start after optional whitespace).

findings.claim: The harness has no positive-control fixture, so a checker regression that reports all six rule names unconditionally (or on any input) would pass the negative test; the only passing-path control is incidental ordering in `ci-grep-gates.sh`.
findings.evidence: Every spawnSync assertion in `test-platform-adapters-negative.mjs` checks `status !== 0` plus output content; no invocation asserts that a clean tree exits 0, while the real-tree pass in `scripts/ci-grep-gates.sh` only guards the current repo state, not checker behavior on arbitrary clean input.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a minimal clean fixture directory and assert the gate exits 0 on it before running the violating fixtures.
